issues.problem: The design says to reuse getLatestPublishedId for the head reopen target while the new spec requires latest published non-archived, but the actual getLatestPublishedId query filters only periodStatus='published' and does not exclude archived rows. If the newest published row is archived, a head cannot reopen the newest non-archived published period because the equality check resolves to the archived id and then rejects every non-archived candidate.
issues.fix: Specify and test a non-archived latest-published resolver for lifecycle authz, or change the shared resolver and its durable viewer expectations deliberately.

issues.problem: The spec requires missing reportId to map to NOT_FOUND, but the tasks only add a typed error for out-of-scope/archived denials; the current service throws generic Error for missing reports in both publish and reopen, which mapDomainError will continue surfacing as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR unless the implementation invents an unstated not-found error.
issues.fix: Add an explicit task to introduce a typed PeriodNotFoundError and replace both generic missing-report throws before adding the NOT_FOUND mapper branch.

issues.problem: The design permits reusing the existing PeriodAccessError family for scope denials, but that class currently also represents state/policy failures such as already-published, non-published reopen, disabled reopen, and expired reopen window. Mapping PeriodAccessError wholesale to FORBIDDEN would change unrelated lifecycle/policy errors; not mapping it leaves the new scope denials at 500.
issues.fix: Require distinct typed errors or discriminated error codes for scope/archived and not-found cases, and map only those exact cases.

notes: Read proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md, delta spec, cited API/web code, and touched durable specs; openspec validate "scope-period-lifecycle-authz" --strict passed.

issues.problem: listExecutions is only scoped by whether the rule's report has at least one in-scope section, but current executions are rule-wide and AdminReminderExecution exposes recipientEmail/dedupeKey. On a normal shared report containing group-A and group-B sections, a group-A head would pass the proposed rule check and still receive group-B execution rows from RemindersPrismaRepository.listExecutions(ruleId).
issues.fix: Require listExecutions to filter returned executions to in-scope recipient emails, or reject non-admin listing for mixed-scope report-wide rules unless the repository/service can enforce recipient scope.

issues.problem: Task 3.2 says to throw FORBIDDEN whenever leadId resolves to zero in-scope draft sections, but that also covers an in-scope lead with no draft section or an already-submitted section. The existing UI has a no-matching-section success state for this case, so the task conflates authorization failure with a valid no-pending-work result.
issues.fix: Check lead existence/group scope separately from draft status; throw FORBIDDEN only for out-of-scope leads and preserve no-matching-section for in-scope leads with no draft section.

notes: openspec validate --strict passes, but the proposal misses recipient-level scoping for execution history and over-tightens a dispatchPending edge case.

issues.problem: The change deliberately makes Bull Board's requireHead async and adds Prisma/SessionRevocation checks, but the existing durable dependency-currency spec still requires the Bull Board route to have no auth-middleware change and says requireHead must remain byte-identical to the pre-upgrade form. The proposal declares no modified capabilities, so implementing it would violate an existing spec.
issues.fix: Add a MODIFIED delta for dependency-currency that supersedes the byte-identical auth-middleware clause for this security hardening while preserving route/base path/queue wiring.

issues.problem: The design says mountBullBoard should construct a SessionRevocationService and treats onModuleDestroy cleanup as per-instance, but a manually constructed service resolved outside Nest DI will not have its lifecycle hook called by Nest. This adds another unmanaged ioredis client and can leave shutdown/test handles open.
issues.fix: Resolve the exported SessionRevocationService from Nest DI via _app.get(SessionRevocationService) or explicitly register cleanup for the manually constructed instance.

notes: Read proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md, the spec delta, cited trpc/bull-board/auth/revocation code, and touched existing specs; openspec validate enforce-deactivation-pdf-bullboard --strict passes, but semantic spec conflict remains.

issues.problem: The change tells the publication path to keep a `status === "published"` fast-path rejection and use `status != "published"` as the CAS guard, while the same spec requires `review.publish` to target the DB-resolved open/reopened period. Reopened periods are intentionally `status="published"`, `periodState="open"`, `periodStatus="reopened"`, so `review.publish` would reject or zero-match the exact reopened period it is supposed to publish.
issues.fix: Base `review.publish` publishability/CAS on `periodStatus != "published"` and carry `periodStatus` through the publication repository/service result instead of using legacy `status`.

issues.problem: The modified telemetry requirement governs `PublicationService.publishReport` and requires the `from` label to be the actual prior `periodStatus`, including `reopened`, but the publication read model only exposes legacy `status` and the task tests only mention a newer open period / redundant counters. That leaves no explicit implementation or failing test proving `review.publish` can emit `from:"reopened"` instead of retaining the current hardcoded `from:"open"`.
issues.fix: Add a `review.publish` characterization/contract test for a DB-resolved reopened period and require the guarded publication write to return the prior `periodStatus` used for the counter label.

notes: Read the full change directory, checked touched durable specs, and validated the change structurally with `openspec validate "make-publish-atomic" --strict`.

issues.problem: The plan rewires only SnapshotAdminService, ProjectAdminService, and ReminderAdminService, but PeriodAdminService.upsertPeriod still does getSnapshot -> saveSnapshot. Since saveSnapshot writes groups, users, projects, periods, and reminder rules, a period edit can still overwrite stale copies of unrelated collections even after destructive deletes are removed.
issues.fix: Add a targeted period upsert path or explicitly rewrite PeriodAdminService.upsertPeriod so it cannot call full saveSnapshot for a single-period edit.

issues.problem: The change spec says whole-snapshot destructive reconcile is removed, but the design leaves saveSnapshot's real restore-removal contract unresolved until implementation. That makes the normative behavior of saveSnapshot impossible to review or test: additive-only restore and explicit deletion-set restore are materially different contracts.
issues.fix: Choose the saveSnapshot removal contract in the spec/design now and add scenarios/tests for absent users, projects, and reminder rules under that contract.

issues.problem: The proposal names the auto-period scheduler racing manual/admin/login creation as one of the duplicate-period races, but the task/spec coverage only adds P2002 handling to admin create/update and ensureWeeklyReport; PeriodCreatorScheduler still does a bare report.create, so after the index lands the named scheduler race becomes an unhandled Prisma error instead of a graceful/idempotent outcome.
issues.fix: Add a requirement/task/test for PeriodCreatorScheduler to catch Report_one_open_per_boundary P2002 and treat the tick as already-created/re-read-or-skip, rethrowing unrelated errors.

issues.problem: The new partial unique index is not only an insert guard; it also rejects updates that move an existing row into periodState='open'. The design explicitly excludes transition-writer changes, but existing scheduled->open, reopen, and unarchive paths can all write periodState='open' with no precheck/catch, so valid states allowed by the spec (a non-open row sharing a boundary with an open row) can later turn into unhandled P2002s on lifecycle actions.
issues.fix: Extend the change to cover every writer that can transition a Report into periodState='open' with either a domain-level overlap error or an intentional skip/re-read path, plus tests for those P2002 cases.

issues.problem: Task 5.2 tells implementers to run pnpm lint:md, but the root scripts contain lint, format, and format:check only; the repo convention says Markdown is formatted, not markdown-linted, so this verification step is currently a dead command.
issues.fix: Replace pnpm lint:md with pnpm format:check for OpenSpec markdown plus openspec validate period-uniqueness-db-constraint --strict.

notes: Reviewed the full change directory, cited product code, touched durable specs, and ran openspec validate period-uniqueness-db-constraint --strict successfully.

issues.problem: The plan says to filter records/per-stage statuses only, but the returned ReportSectionReadModel also exposes projects and referencedProjects. The mapper builds projects from all unarchived author stage assignments, including productName, trafficLight, ownedStages, and stageSet, so an unshared product can still leak even after items/risks/decisions are filtered.
issues.fix: Require and test filtering section.projects and referencedProjects to the shared-product set, including their ownedStages/stageSet/status-derived fields.

issues.problem: D3 accepts an empty shared set as an authorized empty section, but the existing getByPeriod gate still uses hasSharedProduct, which does not exclude archived projects, while getCrossAuthorContent defines co-ownership through shared non-archived products. A lead sharing only an archived product could still read foreign section metadata/status after the proposed change.
issues.fix: Replace the getByPeriod authorization gate with the same shared non-archived viewer/author product query used for filtering, and deny/fall back when that set is empty.

issues.problem: The requirement says the filter must cover per-stage statuses, but the contract-test requirement and tasks only assert items, risks, and decisions plus own/head full reads. A stage/status leak could pass the proposed test suite.
issues.fix: Add explicit contract-test assertions for unshared product projects/ownedStages/stageSet or whatever field carries per-stage status in getByPeriod's read model.

notes: openspec validate --strict passes, but semantic review found proposal/code mismatches that should be fixed before implementation.

issues.problem: The proposal claims to replace the reachable bare Error sites in fillFrom, but it omits the source-section guards: missing source currently throws `Source section ... not found.` and forged cross-author source throws `Can only fill from your own section.` as bare Error, so a covered security-relevant forged request would still map to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR after implementation.
issues.fix: Add source-section missing and source-owner-denied cases to the requirements, design table, tasks, mapper expectations, and contract tests using LeadFormDomainError and LeadFormAccessError respectively.

issues.problem: The delta requires `trpc.error-mapper.test.ts` to be exhaustive for every domain error class handled by mapDomainError, but the tasks only add tests for the three new classes; current mapper branches also lack direct coverage for existing classes such as LeadFormAccessError, ReportSectionAccessError, and AdminPeriodNotFoundError.
issues.fix: Either narrow the requirement to the new classes or add explicit task items/test cases for every existing mapper-handled domain error class.

issues.problem: The task says to import `AdminPeriodNotFoundError` from `../admin-shared.js` in `admin-period.queries.ts`, but that file is already in `apps/api/src/modules/admin`, so the relative import should be `./admin-shared.js`; the written path would not resolve.
issues.fix: Change the task to import from `./admin-shared.js`, or import via the existing admin facade if preserving that convention is preferred.

notes: Reviewed the entire change directory, the cited mapper/throw sites, and relevant existing specs. Main gap is that fillFrom has source-section bare Error paths not covered by the proposal.
